newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ex-Stockholm air cargo rates ease in summer lull.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Stockholm air cargo rates ease in summer lull.

text.p: Air cargo rates from Sweden fell across the board in the summer holiday doldrums, a Reuters survey of airlines and forwarders showed, as airlines said they planned to add still more cargo space to the market.
Options for cheaper seasonal rates were going around on the market, market players said. Volumes have been steady until now but should quiet down in the second half of the month.
The 72-hour strike last week by British Airways Plc's cabin crew had little effect on the ex-Stockholm market.
Swiss forwarding group Panalpina said it would step up its five-times weekly flights to Luxembourg with its DC-8 to include Saturdays from July 19.
South Korean air carrier Asiana Airlines, which launched non-stop flights from Germany, Belgium and Austria at the end of May, has set up regularly scheduled trucks from all over the Nordic region.
Thai Airways International Ltd's cargo division said it plans a Boeing 747-200 freighter service from August 5 through Paris, Dubai, Stockholm and Osaka.

The number of plant closures in Sweden has diminished in recent years, but there still is a noticeable slowing in July. Most shippers said they had been busy as manufacturers wind down business ahead of the holiday period.

"Most of them are operational but not at 100 percent. The clients are shipping around the world so I can't say any specific areas are affected by the situation," said Lufthansa Cargo regional director Sweden Sven Ahlberg.
Rates to New York's JFK eased marginally, to 9.98 crowns from 10.10 crowns per kg for a 100 kg shipment, to 10.63 crowns from 11.40 crowns to Chicago and to 11.76 crowns from 13.00 to Los Angeles.
There were rumours of price dumping to New York.

To Hong Kong the rate was 12.91 crowns compared to 13.60 at the time of the last market report in the mid-May and to Shanghai the rate was about the same as to Hong Kong, 12.88 crowns compared to 13.60.
The rate to Japan was 18.75 crowns compared to 19.90 and to Bangkok 12.86 crowns compared to 13.20.
"From our point-of-view the Japan market has gone down," said one freight forwarder who asked to be unnamed.
So far Asiana Airlines's presence on the ex-Stockholm market had not made a noticeable impact on rates, market players said.
The rate to Johannesburg fell to 18.75 crowns from 20.10 crowns. To London it edged down to 7.08 crowns from 7.45 crowns and to Paris was steady at 7.25 crowns.
